city_center.name: Old Town Albuquerque
city_center.landmark: Old Town Plaza + San Felipe de Neri Church (1706 townsite), Sandia Mountains on the eastern skyline
city_center.notes: Old Town is the 1706 original townsite, a Pueblo Revival / Territorial adobe district; the Sandia Mountains glow watermelon-pink at sunset ('Sandia' = watermelon). Downtown Growers Market (Robinson Park) is the summer gathering anchor. sources: Old Town Albuquerque (en.wikipedia.org); Sandia Mountains (en.wikipedia.org).

cultural_notes: 'red or green?' is the official New Mexico state question; Albuquerque leans red-chile (posole, carne adovada) vs the green-chile south (source: New Mexico state question, newmexico.org)

Pueblo Revival is the region's signature architecture: adobe or stone, flat roofs, rounded corners, thick walls, vigas and latillas -- codified by Santa Fe architect John Gaw Meem, the 'official' campus style at UNM (source: Pueblo architecture + Scholes Hall, en.wikipedia.org)

Albuquerque is a major urban hub for the Navajo Nation and Pueblo communities; pinon-harvest is a fall high-desert tradition (source: market-languages.json Navajo reason; frontier-gaps.json pinon cross-promo). tribal partnership references stay consent-gated -- no fabricated endorsement
the Albuquerque International Balloon Fiesta (early October) is a signature civic ritual and dawn-sky visual cue (INFERRED civic-ritual framing from region knowledge -- verify before production use)

Sandia watermelon-pink grounded in the range name + sunset granite glow (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandia_Mountains; albuquerque.com). turquoise is a New Mexico signature accent. hex values are perceptual approximations, not sampled -- flag for brand-fit review against fixed brand palette.
